title: dedicated: add autoscaling burst controls and fleet utilization reporting
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience short user-driven traffic spikes that temporarily exceed reserved steady-state capacity and lead to queueing and increased tail latency. This PR introduces configurable burst controls (burst window, max burst tokens, cooldown) at the fleet and route level and adds a fleet utilization reporting pipeline so operators can measure burst consumption versus steady throughput. Changes include API surface for burst policy, scheduler enforcement, metrics emission, and UI telemetry hooks. Checklist: [x] API + protobufs for burst policy; [x] scheduler enforcement and admission checks; [x] utilization reporter and prometheus metrics; [x] integration tests and perf canary; [x] console dashboard wiring; Testing notes: unit tests for admission logic, integration test exercising burst window behavior under synthetic load, perf canary run on staging fleet. Related: ENG-2345 autoscale policy revamp, ENG-2390 capacity accounting work.
commits_summary: 4 commits: 1) api: add BurstPolicy protobuf and validation, 2) scheduler: implement burst token bucket enforcement and cooldown, 3) telemetry: emit dedicated_fleet_burst_{used,available,window_seconds} and utilization aggregation job, 4) console: expose per-fleet burst usage chart and alert rule template.
changed_files_summary: Modified: pkg/dedicated/api.proto, pkg/scheduler/burst_control.go, pkg/scheduler/admission.go, services/telemetry/reporting/usage_aggregator.go, internal/metrics/metrics_registry.go, web/console/src/components/fleet/BurstChart.tsx, tests/integration/dedicated_burst_test.go, docs/operation/dedicated_burst_controls.md and small updates to CI and deployment manifests.
ci_checks: perf/regression: initial run flagged minor GC spike -> tuned buffer allocation -> pass
review_comments: Alex Martinez: Can we make the default burst window conservative (30s) to avoid surprise cost deltas? Please add a comment in api.proto explaining rationale.
Priya Nair: Good point. Default set to 30s and rationale added to api.proto comments; unit test added to validate default behavior.
Jordan Li: Scheduler change looks good. Please ensure that admission failures emit a distinct metric so SRE can alert on repeated rejections.
Priya Nair: Added dedicated_fleet_burst_rejections counter and docs for alerting; added integration test to assert counter increments on rejection.
Marta Kovacs: The utilization reporter aggregation is O(N) over active routes; are we comfortable with the cost at 1m resolution? Consider incremental aggregation.
Priya Nair: Switched to incremental aggregation window and added a stress test showing negligible CPU impact in 1m buckets.
Release manager: Please include migration note for fleets that had custom autoscale policies.
Priya Nair: Added migration guide in docs/operation/dedicated_burst_controls.md describing default behavior and recommended rollout steps.
release_notes: Added configurable burst controls for Dedicated fleets: burst window, max burst tokens, cooldown period.
Added fleet utilization reporting metrics and a console chart to track burst consumption and steady throughput.
Backwards compatible: default burst policy is conservative (30s window, low tokens) to avoid sudden cost or capacity changes.
Operators should review alerting guidance in docs and update runbooks if relying on steady-state limits.
